entries.label: What is Web Accessibility
entries.quote: Web accessibility means that websites, tools, and technologies are designed and developed so that people with disabilities can use them.

entries.label: Accessibility in Context
entries.quote: Accessibility is essential for developers and organizations that want to create high-quality websites and web tools, and not exclude people from using their products and services.
entries.context: Accessibility is essential for developers and organizations that want to create high-quality websites and web tools, and not exclude people from using their products and services.

entries.label: Accessibility is Important for Individuals, Businesses, Society
entries.quote: That is, the accessibility barriers to print, audio, and visual media can be much more easily overcome through web technologies.
entries.context: The Web offers the possibility of unprecedented access to information and interaction for many people with disabilities. That is, the accessibility barriers to print, audio, and visual media can be much more easily overcome through web technologies.

entries.label: Accessibility is Important for Individuals, Businesses, Society
entries.quote: Web accessibility is required by law in many situations.
entries.context: Web accessibility is required by law in many situations.

entries.label: Making the Web Accessible
entries.quote: Web accessibility depends on several components working together, including web technologies, web browsers and other "user agents", authoring tools, and websites.
entries.context: Web accessibility depends on several components working together, including web technologies, web browsers and other "user agents", authoring tools, and websites.

entries.label: Making the Web Accessible
entries.quote: The W3C Web Accessibility Initiative ( WAI ) develops technical specifications, guidelines, techniques, and supporting resources that describe accessibility solutions.
entries.context: The W3C Web Accessibility Initiative ( WAI ) develops technical specifications, guidelines, techniques, and supporting resources that describe accessibility solutions. These are considered international standards for web accessibility; for example, WCAG 2.2 is also an ISO standard: ISO/ IEC 40500.
